item.title: Visualize Pull Requests with Kanvas Snapshot
item.description:
Kanvas Snapshot posts a picture of your infrastructure as a comment on each GitHub pull request. Reviewers see which components a Kubernetes manifest, Docker Compose file, or Helm chart defines, and how they connect, before they read the YAML. The comment updates on every push to the pull request.

The snapshot runs in a GitHub Actions workflow on GitHub-hosted runners. It never touches your cluster. For how a snapshot is built and what it can and cannot do, see Kanvas Snapshot.

item.title: Kanvas Snapshot
item.description:
Kanvas Snapshot turns an infrastructure-as-code file into a picture of the design it describes. It runs as a GitHub workflow or as a Helm plugin, not in the Kanvas canvas, so reviewers see the shape of a change (which components exist and how they connect) without reading YAML or opening Kanvas.

A snapshot is standalone. It never connects to your cluster and never deploys anything. It reads the file you point it at, builds a design from it, and renders that design to an image.
